fieldNotes:
What this is. Besides the pictures from space, the site can show the aerial photographs of swisstopo's special flights (Spezialbefliegungen) for a year: orthophotos (aerial photographs corrected to the geometry of a map) made from images of an airborne camera, flown on the dates in the table. They are not satellite pictures and not the yearly SWISSIMAGE mosaic: each is one flight on one day, in summer or early autumn, and covers only the part of the glacier the flight reached. You switch them on with swisstopo special flight in the layer menu of the map and of the 3D view (one year only). A small dock under the year lists that year's flights, each with its own switch, and a second switch for the near-infrared lines where the same flight has them.

What exists for Findelgletscher

14 flights with natural-colour orthophotos touching the glacier outline of SGI 2023 (13.17 km²), from 2016 to 2025. The column Share of the 2023 glacier outline covered is computed here: the share of the 2023 outline (counted on a 20 m grid) where that flight has valid pixels; the flights of one year together cover at most 99.5 %. The other columns are as the swisstopo catalogue states them (the camera and the pixel size of the orthophoto, in metres).

Which flights, and how they are drawn

  • Selection. Only natural-colour (RGB) and near-infrared orthophotos of a flight whose valid pixels touch the 2023 outline (at least 1 % of its area) are used. Rapid-mapping mosaics (ram-*) are not used, and a mosaic labelled RGB that is false colour in disguise is dropped. A year without a flight has no picture.
  • Resolution. Nothing of the flights is stored with the site. The map and the 3D view cut their tiles live from swisstopo's own files, natural colour and near infrared alike, asking only for the blocks they need; the browser decodes them. When a flight is switched on, a quick coarse picture (the 3.2 m overview) appears first and is then replaced by the sharpness the zoom needs: 0.8 m at zoom 17, 0.4 m at zoom 18, and at zoom 19 and 20 as sharp as the file itself (pixel size in the table). While a flight is on, the map may go to zoom 20; the 3D view draws it on a texture twice as wide and as high as normal.
  • Edges and colour. The border of every orthophoto is trimmed by 12 m (it carries dark no-data fringes); black pixels are no data. Flights of one year are not colour-matched, so seams show where two flights meet, as do changes in light and snow between days. Near infrared is shown as near infrared, red, green (false colour), with one stretch (2 to 98 percent of the values, computed) for each flight.
  • Position. The map places the live tiles with swisstopo's approximate WGS84 to LV95 formula, which swisstopo states as accurate to about 1 m; on the Aletsch area it agrees with PROJ to about 0.1 m (computed). The accuracy statement of swisstopo for these orthophotos was not read.

What it is not

  • It is not the yearly ice surface of these notes. The 3D ice surface of a year is the surface on the day of the Sentinel-2 picture (see the chapters above); an aerial photograph shows the glacier on its own flight day, which can be weeks away.
  • It is not complete: a flight reaches only part of the glacier, so most of the glacier has no special-flight picture in any year (see the column Share of the 2023 glacier outline covered).

Source and terms

swisstopo, Spezialbefliegungen (collection ch.swisstopo.spezialbefliegungen), 14 catalogue items used here (4 flights with near-infrared lines). Terms of use read on 2026-11-06 at swisstopo.admin.ch/ogd-conditions: the free geodata may be used, distributed and made accessible, also commercially, and a reference to the source is mandatory.
